That suppresses genuinely novel members when a duplicate and a novel finding are clustered together by single-linkage within the current round. Evidence is the loop: `is_novel` starts true, but the first member with similarity above `_tau_sim()` to any prior finding sets `is_novel = False` and breaks out before checking whether other class members have no prior match.

Consequences: `kappa_set()` numerator omits `B`’s novel severity; `_veto()` fails to veto if `B` is high severity; `kappa_rate()` undercounts novel discovery; `converged()` may terminate despite a new high-severity issue.  
ANALYSE: HARD correctness constraint. Premises: current-round classes are formed by single-linkage, so a class may contain both a prior-matching member and a member with no prior match; novelty for convergence/veto must not hide a new issue merely because it is clustered with a duplicate; the current implementation uses universal non-match semantics. Derivation: existence of one prior-matching member is not sufficient to prove all class members are prior-known. Therefore, the current code is silently wrong for mixed classes. Conclusion: CONFIRMED.
